avoid.reason: Very safe; around Dotonbori/Minami avoid nightlife touts and inflated-bill bars

hood_desc: The vibrant southern entertainment hub around Dotonbori, famed for dazzling neon, street food and buzzing nightlife. Ideal for foodies and visitors wanting Osaka's lively downtown energy.
The sleek northern business and shopping district around Osaka Station, with department stores, skyscrapers and underground malls. Best for travelers wanting modern convenience and transport links.
A retro, gritty old-school neighborhood dominated by the Tsutenkaku tower and cheap kushikatsu eateries. Suits those curious about nostalgic, working-class Osaka atmosphere.
A district anchored by the historic Shitennoji temple, a large park, zoo and the towering Abeno Harukas building. Great for families and visitors mixing culture with shopping.
A premier shopping street and district lined with covered arcades, boutiques and department stores. Perfect for dedicated shoppers who want everything from luxury to bargains.

water.note: Tap water is treated to a very high standard and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Buy an ICOCA IC card (about ¥2,000/$13, including a refundable deposit) from station machines, or tap a contactless Visa/Mastercard/Amex directly at Osaka Metro gates. Base fares start around ¥180 (~$1.20) and rise with distance.
transit.hours: Trains and the metro run about 5am to midnight with no regular overnight service; night buses and taxis fill the gap after last trains.

landmarks: Osaka Castle
A monumental restored 16th-century castle set in a moated park, iconic for its gold-trimmed green roofs against the skyline.
Dotonbori
Osaka's neon-lit canal-side entertainment district famous for the giant illuminated Glico Running Man sign and vibrant nightlife photos.
Umeda Sky Building
A striking twin-tower skyscraper connected by a floating rooftop observatory offering panoramic city views at sunset.
Shitennoji Temple
One of Japan's oldest Buddhist temples, prized for its symmetrical pagoda and gate architecture in a traditional garden setting.
Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
One of the world's largest aquariums, known for its massive central tank with whale sharks, a favorite for unique underwater-style shots.
Universal Studios Japan
A theme park famous for its elaborate themed lands and photogenic entrance globe and Hollywood-style facades.
Tsutenkaku Tower
A retro-futuristic tower landmark of the Shinsekai district, iconic for its illuminated exterior and old-Osaka atmosphere.
Sumiyoshi Taisha
An ancient Shinto shrine renowned for its distinctive Sumiyoshi-zukuri architecture and arched drum bridge, a classic photo subject.
Namba Yasaka Shrine
A small shrine famous for its giant lion-head-shaped stage structure, one of Osaka's most unusual photo spots.
Abeno Harukas
Japan's tallest skyscraper, offering a sweeping observation-deck view over Osaka that makes for dramatic cityscape photography.

dom.op: JR West (JR-WEST Online Train Reservation / e5489)

train.note: Japan is an island nation with no international trains. Domestic rail is superb: book JR West trains online in English, or use smartEX (https://smart-ex.jp/en/) for Tokaido-Sanyo-Kyushu Shinkansen tickets from Shin-Osaka to Tokyo, Hiroshima and Fukuoka.

bus.note: No international buses exist from Japan. Long-distance highway and overnight buses leave Osaka for Tokyo, Hiroshima, Kanazawa and beyond - main operators are Willer Express (https://willerexpress.com/en/) and West JR Bus (https://www.nishinihonjrbus.co.jp/).

ferry.note: The Osaka-Shanghai passenger ferries (Shanghai Ferry's Su Zhou Hao and Japan-China International Ferry's Xin Jian Zhen) briefly restarted in mid-2025 but passenger carriage was suspended again in December 2025 amid Japan-China tensions and remains unconfirmed as of July 2026 - check https://www.shinganjin.com/en/ before planning. Domestic overnight ferries do run from Osaka Nanko: Ferry Sunflower to Beppu and Shibushi in Kyushu (https://www.ferry-sunflower.co.jp/en/) and Orange Ferry to Shikoku.

half.name: Kyoto
half.blurb: Japan's old capital draws crowds for its golden temples, wooden shrines, and traditional geisha districts.

half.name: Nara
half.blurb: People come to wander ancient temples and meet the tame deer roaming Nara Park freely.

half.name: Kobe
half.blurb: This stylish port city is beloved for its famous beef, waterfront, and sparkling mountaintop night views.

half.name: Himeji
half.blurb: Visitors travel here to see Himeji Castle, Japan's grandest and best-preserved original feudal fortress.

half.name: Mount Koya (Koyasan)
half.blurb: This sacred mountain temple town offers Buddhist lodging, misty forests, and a vast atmospheric cemetery.

half.name: Uji
half.blurb: Famous for its green matcha tea, Uji also holds the beautiful Byodo-in Phoenix Hall temple.
